title: Fractional Knapsack - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given two arrays, val[] and wt[], representing the values and weights of n items, respectively, and an integer capacity representing the maximum weight a knapsack can hold.

Find the maximum total value that can be obtained without exceeding the knapsack's capacity. Items can be divided into fractions if required.

Examples:

Input: val[] = [60, 100, 120], wt[] = [10, 20, 30], capacity = 50
Output: 240 
Explanation: We will take the items of weight 10kg and 20kg and 2/3 fraction of 30kg. 
Hence total value will be 60 + 100 + (2/3) * 120 = 240.

Input: val[] = [500], wt[] = [30], capacity = 10
Output: 166.667
Explanation: The capacity is 10kg, so we will take 1/3 fraction of the 30kg item. Hence, total value will be (1/3) * 500 = 166.667.

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • [Naive Approach] Select Items Based on Weight or Value
  • Greedy by Value-to-Weight Ratio - O(nlogn) Time and O(n) Space

[Naive Approach] Select Items Based on Weight or Value

Selecting items based only on their weight or total value does not always maximize the total value.

Case 1: Picking the items with smaller weights first

Consider val[] = [10, 10, 10, 100], wt[] = [10, 10, 10, 30], and capacity = 30.

  • If we select the three items with smaller weights first, the total value is 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.
  • However, selecting the item weighing 30 gives a value of 100, which is optimal.

Thus, selecting items based only on their weights does not always maximize the total value.

Case 2: Picking items with larger value first

Consider val[] = [10, 10, 10, 20], wt[] = [10, 10, 10, 30], and capacity = 30.

  • If we select the item with the highest value first, we get a total value of 20.
  • However, selecting the three items weighing 10 each gives a total value of 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 , which is optimal.

Thus, selecting items based only on their values does not always maximize the total value.

Greedy by Value-to-Weight Ratio - O(nlogn) Time and O(n) Space

The idea is to select items in decreasing order of their value-to-weight ratio, as items with a higher ratio provide more value per unit of weight.

  • Calculate the value-to-weight ratio for each item using val[i] / wt[i].
  • Sort the items in decreasing order of their ratios.
  • Traverse the sorted items. If an item fits within the remaining capacity, take it completely, add its value to the total, and reduce the remaining capacity.
  • If an item does not fit completely, take the fraction that fits and add its proportional value to the total.
  • Stop when the knapsack is full or all items have been considered.
C++ 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

// Comparison function to sort items based on value/weight ratio
static bool compare(vector<int>& a, vector<int>& b)
{
    double a1 = (1.0 * a[0]) / a[1];
    double b1 = (1.0 * b[0]) / b[1];

    return a1 > b1;
}

double fractionalKnapsack(vector<int>& val, vector<int>& wt, int capacity)
{
    int n = val.size();

    // Create 2D vector to store value and weight
    vector<vector<int>> items(n, vector<int>(2));

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        items[i][0] = val[i];
        items[i][1] = wt[i];
    }

    // Sort items by value-to-weight ratio
    sort(items.begin(), items.end(), compare);

    double res = 0.0;
    int currentCapacity = capacity;

    // Process items in sorted order
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        // Take the complete item
        if (items[i][1] <= currentCapacity)
        {
            res += items[i][0];
            currentCapacity -= items[i][1];
        }
        // Take a fraction of the item
        else
        {
            res += (1.0 * items[i][0] / items[i][1]) * currentCapacity;
            break;
        }
    }

    return res;
}

int main()
{
    vector<int> val = {60, 100, 120};
    vector<int> wt = {10, 20, 30};
    int capacity = 50;

    cout << fractionalKnapsack(val, wt, capacity) << endl;

    return 0;
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

// Function to compare two items based on value-to-weight ratio
int compare(const void *a, const void *b)
{
    const float *itemA = (const float *)a;
    const float *itemB = (const float *)b;

    float ratioA = itemA[0] / itemA[1];
    float ratioB = itemB[0] / itemB[1];

    if (ratioA < ratioB)
        return 1;
    if (ratioA > ratioB)
        return -1;

    return 0;
}

float fractionalKnapsack(float val[], float wt[], int capacity, int n)
{
    // Create an array to store value and weight
    float items[n][2];

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        items[i][0] = val[i];
        items[i][1] = wt[i];
    }

    // Sort items based on value-to-weight ratio
    qsort(items, n, sizeof(items[0]), compare);

    float res = 0.0;
    float currentCapacity = capacity;

    // Process items in sorted order
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        // Take the complete item
        if (items[i][1] <= currentCapacity)
        {
            res += items[i][0];
            currentCapacity -= items[i][1];
        }
        // Take a fraction of the item
        else
        {
            res += (items[i][0] / items[i][1]) * currentCapacity;
            // Knapsack is full
            break;
        }
    }

    return res;
}

int main()
{
    float val[] = {60, 100, 120};
    float wt[] = {10, 20, 30};
    int capacity = 50;

    int n = sizeof(val) / sizeof(val[0]);

    printf("%.2f", fractionalKnapsack(val, wt, capacity, n));

    return 0;
}

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Comparator;

class GFG {

    // Comparison function to sort items based on value/weight ratio
    static class ItemComparator implements Comparator<int[]> {
        public int compare(int[] a, int[] b) {
            double a1 = (1.0 * a[0]) / a[1];
            double b1 = (1.0 * b[0]) / b[1];
            return Double.compare(b1, a1);
        }
    }

    static double fractionalKnapsack(int[] val, int[] wt, int capacity) {
        int n = val.length;

        // Create 2D array to store value and weight
        // items[i][0] = value, items[i][1] = weight
        int[][] items = new int[n][2];

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            items[i][0] = val[i];
            items[i][1] = wt[i];
        }

        // Sort items based on value-to-weight ratio in descending order
        Arrays.sort(items, new ItemComparator());

        double res = 0.0;
        int currentCapacity = capacity;

        // Process items in sorted order
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {

            // If we can take the entire item
            if (items[i][1] <= currentCapacity) {
                res += items[i][0];
                currentCapacity -= items[i][1];
            }

            // Otherwise take a fraction of the item
            else {
                res += (1.0 * items[i][0] / items[i][1]) * currentCapacity;

                // Knapsack is full
                break;
            }
        }

        return res;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] val = {60, 100, 120};
        int[] wt = {10, 20, 30};
        int capacity = 50;

        System.out.println(fractionalKnapsack(val, wt, capacity));
    }
}

def fractionalKnapsack(val, wt, capacity):
    n = len(val)

    # Create list to store value and weight
    # items[i][0] = value, items[i][1] = weight
    items = [[val[i], wt[i]] for i in range(n)]

    # Sort items based on value-to-weight ratio in descending order
    items.sort(key=lambda x: x[0]/x[1], reverse=True)

    res = 0.0
    currentCapacity = capacity

    # Process items in sorted order
    for i in range(n):

        # If we can take the entire item
        if items[i][1] <= currentCapacity:
            res += items[i][0]
            currentCapacity -= items[i][1]

        # Otherwise take a fraction of the item
        else:
            res += (1.0 * items[i][0] / items[i][1]) * currentCapacity

            # Knapsack is full
            break

    return res
